# Project History — retired-document index

> Compact index of historical release notes and audits. Current product decisions live in `docs/MASTER_STATUS.md`; the chronological release log lives in `docs/CHANGELOG.md`. This file preserves key references and historical facts without duplicating full reports.

## Historical content and quality audits

- **TOEIC Distractor & Answer-Uniqueness Audit** — historical editorial audit — Reviewed 132 questions for distractor quality and whether each item had **exactly one defensible answer**. This was a scoped historical review, not an approval of the current reserve queue or a blanket certification of all later batches. See the retained audit and release reports in `docs/reports/` where available.
- **Listening/Reading reserve review** — later release work created a separate item-level independent-review handoff. The current 280-item queue is tracked in `docs/reports/TOEIC_INDEPENDENT_REVIEW_QUEUE_v2.95.21.md`; queue membership is not reviewer approval or Mock eligibility.
- **Historical pronunciation and glossary work** — source-backed US IPA and related-term gloss batches remain documented in their versioned provenance ledgers and reports. Newly added lookup records are provisional until independent lexical review.

## Retired release notes

Earlier release-specific manifests, test reports, command logs, snapshots and batch checklists are historical evidence. Their recorded results apply only to the version and scope named in each report; they do not imply that remote CI, deployment, browser/device acceptance or independent review passed for the current release.

## Retention rules

- Do not delete canonical vocabulary data, stable IDs, patch payloads, source ledgers, learning content, assets, learner-storage contracts or test fixtures as part of document rotation.
- Keep current and immediately previous release reports active when practical; summarize older material here before archiving or retiring it.
- Preserve review queues and open handoffs while a reviewer decision remains outstanding.

# Foundation A2 Assessment Quality Pass — v2.95.6

## Scope
- 13 core A2 Reading resources + 13 core A2 Listening resources; the new 13 supplementary A2 Listening clips (39 questions) are separately scoped and pending independent review.
- Focused review of within-resource q2/q3 repetition, answer-key uniqueness, four-choice integrity and explicit source traceability for changed/retained focus questions.
- Five question prompts/answer tasks were materially revised; six reviewed question records now carry exact source-evidence pointers.

## Automated integrity results
| Bank | A2 resources | A2 questions | A2 answer positions A/B/C/D |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Reading | 13 | 39 | 10 / 10 / 10 / 9 |
| Listening | 13 | 39 | 10 / 10 / 10 / 9 |

- All A2 questions require four unique choices, a valid answer index, a non-empty prompt and rationale.
- Each A2 resource must have three questions with non-identical q2/q3 correct answers.
- Each source-evidence pointer is checked as an exact substring of its Reading passage or spoken Listening segment.
- Core Reading answer positions remain A/B/C/D = 15/15/15/14; Listening full bank including supplementary practice is A/B/C/D = 25/25/24/24.
- Existing A2 q1/q2 objects remain protected by the v2.75.0 canonical-hash baseline tests.

## Focused changes
| Question | Change |
|---|---|
| `a2-quantities::reading1::q3` | Replaced q3 with a consequence/inference question about the delivery timing and preparation of training materials. |
| `a2-comparisons::reading1::q3` | Replaced q3 with an inference about the customer's priority: dependable, on-time delivery versus lowest price. |
| `a2-obligation-permission::reading1::q3` | Replaced q3 with the separate departure requirement to return the visitor badge. |
| `a2-comparisons::listening1::q3` | Reworded q3 to test the stated reliability/on-time advantage; q2 remains byte-identical to the v2.75.0 baseline. |
| `a2-sequencing-instructions::listening1::q3` | Replaced q3 with the immediately preceding action before preparing the return label. |

## Review boundary
- The pass fixes five identified cases of repeated information and records six exact source pointers. It does not certify every distractor for semantic plausibility or uniqueness.
- The work is an internal single-author review. Independent second-person language review and psychometric validation remain pending.
- The local A2 three-question / 67% rule is a practice threshold only; it is not a CEFR standard, mastery declaration or ETS equivalence.

## Automated audit status
- **PASS** — all registered structural, source-evidence, pair-distinction and answer-position checks passed.

# TOEIC Editorial Evidence Audit — v2.95.36

## Scope and interpretation
- Questions indexed: **582** (295 Listening + 287 Reading).
- Every correct option is linked to its source transcript/passage or an explicit review category.
- Direct/lexical matching is evidence discovery only. It does not prove that distractors are wrong or that a paraphrase/inference is unique.
- Editorial review categories recorded in this source: 6 manually checked low-overlap paraphrase/inference items; 8 Part 1 image/action items; 33 Part 2 response-fit items; 60 Part 5 grammar items; and 32 Part 6 context/cohesion items.
- 161 Listening questions remain reserve-pending-independent-review (Part 1: 1, Part 2: 28, Part 3: 72, Part 4: 60). All reserve answers and distractor uniqueness still require an independent second reviewer; automated evidence mapping does not approve them.
- Reserve traceability gate: **161/161** questions have a transcript evidence pointer that matches the source (0 missing/broken); Part 1 visual evidence note recorded for 1 pending photo item(s).
- Traceable evidence is a review aid, not proof that the key is correct, the distractors are uniquely wrong or the item is ready for Mock.
- These are internal editorial checks, not two-person independent proofreading, psychometric validation or ETS approval.

## Interpretation

- Current eligible pool: a second Full Listening form would reuse 98/100 question IDs (102 eligible total). This improves only after independent approvals are committed. After all reserve approvals, a pair of Full forms would still need three additional Part 1 items for zero repeats.
- This report is not a second-person editorial certification and does not claim native-speaker audio or ETS equivalence.

# Change Manifest — v2.95.13 candidate

## Which version Claude must review

- **Baseline to compare:** v2.95.12 at Git commit `85be68a`.
- **Candidate to review:** v2.95.13 at the final candidate commit recorded in the one-shot handoff.
- **Historical predecessor:** v2.95.11, retained for context only. Claude does not need to re-audit v2.95.11 wholesale; review the v2.95.12 → v2.95.13 delta and verify unchanged contracts where relevant.
- **Release status:** local candidate only; no GitHub push, Actions run or Pages deployment is claimed.

## In-scope changes

| Area | Files/data | Change |
|---|---|---|
| Vocabulary meanings/examples | `data/vocabulary/{B,C,D,E,F,H,M,O,S,V}.json` | 10 existing headwords expanded into 24 sense-linked examples; 20 patch operations; no new headwords |
| Glossary | `data/related-terms.json` | Four additional Vietnamese glosses with Cambridge source URLs |
| Word-family precision | `data/vocabulary/V.json` | `valuable → value (n)` and `valuation → value (v)` aligned to the separated senses |
| Patch provenance | `patches/v2.95.13/`, `patches-related-terms/v2.95.13/`, `data/vocabulary/batch-017.json` … `batch-020.json` | Expect-value, allowlist, stable-ID hash, identity/source guards, dry-run/apply logs and provenance snapshots |
| Regression tests | `tools/tests/test_vocabulary_detail_examples.py`, `tools/tests/test_vocabulary_family_links.py`, `tools/tests/vocabulary-release-integrity.mjs`, `tools/tests/flashcard-senses.mjs` | Verify new source data, `sense_index`, specific POS-linked family meanings, and Flashcard rendering of multi-sense entries |
| Documentation/release | `docs/MASTER_STATUS.md`, `docs/README.md`, `docs/CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/versions/*`, release reports | Version, release notes, evidence, coverage and owner acceptance checklist |

## Explicitly unchanged

- 1,141 canonical IDs, headwords and topic arrays.
- Question banks, question IDs, answer keys, Listening/Reading Mock eligibility and Foundation content.
- Flashcard runtime helper, 10-card maximum contract, Robot Buddy, TTS timing, Service Worker update consent and CSS design-token rules.
- Learner records, IndexedDB database/schema, localStorage keys, migrations and external data transfer.
- No new backend, AI API, GAS, iframe or Cloudflare runtime.

## Required Claude review

1. Compare the baseline and candidate source; verify only the declared files/contracts changed.
2. Re-run each applicable command in the attached test evidence and report exact command, duration, exit code and test count.
3. Inspect all three vocabulary data patches and the related-term patch for `expect.old`, narrow allowlists, stable-ID hash, source references and replay safety.
4. Verify the 10 meanings, 24 examples, four glossary entries and two family-link corrections; distinguish source evidence from editorial approval.
5. Verify Flashcard rendering tests and cross-check that the UI displays sense-linked examples without changing learner storage.
6. Report PASS / FAIL / NOT RUN / INCONCLUSIVE. Do not edit files, change baselines, modify IDs/headwords/topics or push GitHub.

## Review boundary

This package is a code/data review candidate, not a request to approve content automatically. All newly added language material remains pending an independent lexical reviewer. Real browser/device checks remain owner acceptance items.

# Release packaging boundary fix — v2.95.25

## Finding
The packager excluded any directory component named `archive`, which unintentionally removed `docs/archive/PROJECT_HISTORY.md` from FullSource packages. It also did not explicitly exclude `.tmp` artifacts.

## Change
- Exclude only repository-root `archive/` as a directory.
- Preserve nested documentation history such as `docs/archive/`.
- Exclude `.tmp` files alongside `.zip`, `.bundle`, `.log`, and `.pyc`.
- Add package-source tests proving root archive/release/log/temp exclusions and nested documentation history inclusion.

## Validation
- `test_package_source.py`: 3/3 PASS.

## 4. CSS measurement: tool definition and comparison

Claude's supplied v2.95.10 scan reported: 979 unique hex strings / 1,508 uses; 128 font-size values / 918 declarations; 70 non-standard font-weight declarations; 47 radius values; 69 box-shadow values; 114 `!important`; 25 breakpoint values; 34 keyframes.

The new scanner's current v2.95.11 report is:

- Hex strings: 979 unique / 1,508 occurrences.
- `font-size`: 128 unique / 921 declarations.
- `font-weight`: 9 unique / 167 declarations across all CSS; the five allowed numeric values are 400/500/600/700/800.
- `border-radius`: 47 unique / 351 declarations.
- `box-shadow`: 70 unique / 80 declarations.
- Media breakpoint values: 24 unique / 116 occurrences.
- `!important`: 114 occurrences.
- `@keyframes`: 34.

The `font-size` declaration count (921 vs Claude's 918) and breakpoint count (24 vs 25) do not match. They are explicitly reported rather than silently normalized; parser/tokenization definitions differ and need a shared measurement definition before treating the count delta as a source regression. Raw hex count agrees. The box-shadow unique-value metric is 70 in the current scan because the PWA banner now references a shared token; raw value cardinality is not the legacy-warning count.

Ratchet outcome:

- Baseline before banner migration: 2,781 legacy identities / 3,000 occurrences.
- Three exact update-banner violations were resolved and removed from baseline; no new baseline identities were added.
- Current legacy baseline: 2,778 identities / 2,997 occurrences.
- Current new violations: 0.
- Rule hash matches baseline; `RULE-DRIFT` is not present.
- All remaining legacy findings are WARNING, not CI failure. New identities/values, increased occurrences and rule drift fail CI.

# Foundation A2 Assessment Quality Pass — v2.95.25

## Scope
- 13 core A2 Reading resources + 13 core A2 Listening resources; the new 13 supplementary A2 Listening clips (39 questions) are separately scoped and pending independent review.
- Focused review of within-resource q2/q3 repetition, answer-key uniqueness, four-choice integrity and explicit source traceability for changed/retained focus questions.
- Five question prompts/answer tasks were materially revised; six reviewed question records now carry exact source-evidence pointers.

## Automated integrity results
| Bank | A2 resources | A2 questions | A2 answer positions A/B/C/D |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Reading | 13 | 39 | 10 / 10 / 10 / 9 |
| Listening | 13 | 39 | 10 / 10 / 10 / 9 |

- All A2 questions require four unique choices, a valid answer index, a non-empty prompt and rationale.
- Each A2 resource must have three questions with non-identical q2/q3 correct answers.
- Each source-evidence pointer is checked as an exact substring of its Reading passage or spoken Listening segment.
- Core Reading answer positions remain A/B/C/D = 15/15/15/14; Listening full bank including supplementary practice is A/B/C/D = 25/25/24/24.
- Existing A2 q1/q2 objects remain protected by the v2.75.0 canonical-hash baseline tests.

## Focused changes
| Question | Change |
|---|---|
| `a2-quantities::reading1::q3` | Replaced q3 with a consequence/inference question about the delivery timing and preparation of training materials. |
| `a2-comparisons::reading1::q3` | Replaced q3 with an inference about the customer's priority: dependable, on-time delivery versus lowest price. |
| `a2-obligation-permission::reading1::q3` | Replaced q3 with the separate departure requirement to return the visitor badge. |
| `a2-comparisons::listening1::q3` | Reworded q3 to test the stated reliability/on-time advantage; q2 remains byte-identical to the v2.75.0 baseline. |
| `a2-sequencing-instructions::listening1::q3` | Replaced q3 with the immediately preceding action before preparing the return label. |

## Review boundary

## Corrected issues encountered during validation

- The historical `test_vocabulary_detail_examples.py` initially failed because one canonical record includes later provenance fields introduced by a previous release after the old snapshot. The test was narrowed to check every original field while allowing only the known later provenance-field allowlist. It was rerun: **19/19 PASS**. No vocabulary data was changed to satisfy the stale test.
- Historical Batch 027 and current glossary/progress audit tests contained stale release literals. They now validate the current generated backlog/inventory instead of asserting old totals (535/767 or the pre-Batch-037 glossary count). Their final focused suites pass.
- Full `python -m unittest discover -s tools/tests -p 'test_*.py' -v` was attempted but the execution environment timed out before the aggregate suite completed (partial log stopped during `test_patch_data.py`). This is **INCOMPLETE**, not a pass or a test assertion failure. Focused suites listed above completed separately.

- `tools/validate-learning-content.py` checks IDs, choices, answers, explanation presence, Part coverage, passages and image assets. It does not prove semantic correctness; editorial review remains required.

# Foundation A2 Assessment Quality Pass — v2.95.21

## Scope
- 13 core A2 Reading resources + 13 core A2 Listening resources; the new 13 supplementary A2 Listening clips (39 questions) are separately scoped and pending independent review.
- Focused review of within-resource q2/q3 repetition, answer-key uniqueness, four-choice integrity and explicit source traceability for changed/retained focus questions.
- Five question prompts/answer tasks were materially revised; six reviewed question records now carry exact source-evidence pointers.

## Automated integrity results

|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Reading | 13 | 39 | 10 / 10 / 10 / 9 |
| Listening | 13 | 39 | 10 / 10 / 10 / 9 |

- All A2 questions require four unique choices, a valid answer index, a non-empty prompt and rationale.

- Core Reading answer positions remain A/B/C/D = 15/15/15/14; Listening full bank including supplementary practice is A/B/C/D = 25/25/24/24.
- Existing A2 q1/q2 objects remain protected by the v2.75.0 canonical-hash baseline tests.

## Focused changes
| Question | Change |
|---|---|
| `a2-quantities::reading1::q3` | Replaced q3 with a consequence/inference question about the delivery timing and preparation of training materials. |

## Review boundary
- The pass fixes five identified cases of repeated information and records six exact source pointers. It does not certify every distractor for semantic plausibility or uniqueness.
- The work is an internal single-author review. Independent second-person language review and psychometric validation remain pending.
- The local A2 three-question / 67% rule is a practice threshold only; it is not a CEFR standard, mastery declaration or ETS equivalence.

- **PASS** — all registered structural, source-evidence, pair-distinction and answer-position checks passed.

## Queue summary

|---|---:|---:|---|
| Listening Parts 1–4 | 161 | 73 units | Source/key fit, response fit, distractor uniqueness; P1 photo/action match |
| Reading Part 7 | 87 | 22 resources | Document evidence, inference, cross-document links, one-best-answer uniqueness |
| Separate Part 5 sentence completion | 80 | 1 bank | Grammar, naturalness, distractors, translation and one-answer uniqueness |

## Reviewer record

- Reviewer name / role: ____________________________________
- Review date: _____________________________________________
- Review method / reference material: ________________________
- Decision key: `APPROVE` / `REVISE` / `REJECT` (record per item; do not approve a whole batch by default).
- For approval: confirm one defensible key, all distractors are wrong in context, source evidence supports the key, and explanation/translation are accurate.
- For revision: record the exact field and proposed correction; keep the item out of Mock until the correction is retested.

## A. Listening reserve

For Part 2, assess speech act, polarity, indirect response and naturalness. For Parts 3–4, assess transcript support and distractor plausibility. For Part 1, inspect the photo itself as well as the spoken statements.

- Photo: `./assets/listening/part1-office-cleaning.jpg` · Alt: A maintenance worker is sweeping the tiled floor of an office hallway with a broom. A cleaning cart stands nearby.

The image does not show wiping the glass doors, pushing the cart, or arranging chairs. This is an internal visual check, not independent certification.

# Independent assessment of Claude's audit — v2.95.10

**Assessment date:** 2026-11-19  
**Code basis:** v2.95.9 source plus v2.95.10 local commits listed in the release logs.  
**Purpose:** distinguish reproducible measurements, reasonable interpretations and decisions that still require the project owner.

## 1. Executive assessment

Claude's three P0 findings are technically valid and are now addressed in separate commits. The proposed P1/P2 work is directionally sound, but not all numerical estimates should be treated as a release score. The strongest evidence is per-bank inventory, validator output, stable-ID protection, CI coverage and independent-review status—not a single “50% complete” number.

## 2. P0 — findings and disposition

| Claude finding | Independent evidence | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| Vocabulary ID baseline has 928 IDs while current data has 1,141 | Before update: 1,141 unique current IDs, 213 additions and 0 missing. After update: baseline count 1,141; validator reports 0 additions / 0 missing; set SHA-256 `adccbdb4c98872207d2bede7bdc530e1c079bbd8b3679e7e4f6288054c7e404b` | Fixed in its own commit. No vocabulary record was edited. |
| `patch-data.py` accepts protected paths and lacks per-patch whitelist | Test suite now rejects `/id`, `/word`, `/topics` (including descendants), missing `allowedPaths`, and any operation outside the allowlist; the whole batch is rejected. Every operation is written to the JSONL audit log. Historical patch allowlists were added without changing operation payloads. | Fixed in its own commit; 17/17 patch-data tests PASS. An additional safety fix restores original file bytes if the final `APPLIED`/`ROLLED_BACK` audit record fails after the atomic data replacement. |
| Service Worker calls `skipWaiting()` automatically | New worker waits on existing installations; only first install may auto-activate. `SKIP_WAITING` is sent from the explicit update-banner action. Simulator covers failed install/cache preservation, optional failures, namespace cleanup and 404 fallback. | Fixed in its own commit. Two-tab real-browser verification remains NOT TESTED. |

The fixes preserve the user's rules: immutable `/id`, `/word`, `/topics`; expected-old preconditions; dry-run; operation logs; rollback protection; no relaxation of validators; and version updates only via `tools/sync-version.py`.

## 3. Comparison of automated test inventory

- Claude reported 34 JavaScript suites and 427 Python tests on v2.95.8. The current source contains **37 JavaScript `.mjs` suites** and **54 Python test modules / 433 statically declared `test_*` methods** (counted via Python AST). The increase is consistent with three new JS suites since that baseline (`robot-buddy-streaming`, `flashcard-fixed-batch`, `service-worker-update`) and six additional patch-data safety tests.
- The current 37/37 JavaScript suites were executed and passed. The focused Python modules listed in the release test report completed and passed 67 cases. The entire 433-method Python inventory was **not** fully executed in this environment; `test_validator.py` and broad discovery exceeded execution limits. A static test-method count is inventory, not a pass claim.
- Therefore Claude's historical `427 passed in 7.9 seconds` result cannot be independently reproduced from the current environment; it should remain attributed to Claude's Python 3.12.3 / Node 22 execution. The current direct data validator itself passes against all 1,141 vocabulary records.

## 4. P1 — design-system assessment

The supplied counts (979 hex color values, 127 font-size values, 550/650/750/850/950 font weights, 46 border-radius values, 69 box shadows, 114 `!important` occurrences and 25 media-query widths) are plausible static-scan indicators of CSS fragmentation. They are **not independently reproducible from the Claude summary alone**, because the exact scan script, parser rules, selector normalization and treatment of repeated declarations were not supplied. They should be recorded as an initial scan, not a UI-quality score.

What is verified in the project source:

- `design/design-profile.json` contains 54 tokens and is named `Calm Study Blue` (`calm-study-blue`).
- Its status remains `proposed-default-awaiting-user-preferences`; it has not been approved or promoted by this release.
- Responsive behavior has three width boundaries: 640, 850 and 1,199 px. These boundaries form **four responsive bands** (phone, compact tablet, tablet/small desktop, large desktop); they are not four breakpoint boundary values.
- `python tools/sync-design-profile.py --check` passes with 54 tokens and 406 legacy typography-floor selector groups after the PWA banner was changed to use shared font tokens.

Recommendation: approve Calm Study Blue as the initial product design system, subject to actual browser review. Do not bulk-rewrite the CSS before desktop/mobile visual acceptance. Once approved, document token scales and add a selector/property-identified ratchet: legacy violations are warnings, only new violations are errors; then migrate one screen group at a time and tighten the baseline after each reviewed batch. The ratchet must not add exceptions or weaken existing validators.

## 5. P1 — external verification

Local simulation cannot prove GitHub Actions, GitHub Pages cache behavior, first/offline installation, update transitions in two real tabs, iOS Safari/Android Chrome TTS, or physical-device responsive behavior. Keep each item as `Chưa kiểm` until a dated browser/device result is recorded. Do not infer deployment success from a local green validator.

## 6. P2 — actual content coverage

### Vocabulary

- Current canonical vocabulary is 1,141 headwords. Against the project's 3,000 minimum planning target this is 38.0%; against 5,000 it is 22.8%. These are planning ratios, not an official ETS word-list completion score.
- Audited field coverage: US IPA 1,048/1,141 (91.8%); word-family 276 (24.2%); verb forms 329 (28.8%); collocations 971 (85.1%); synonyms 404 (35.4%); antonyms 213 (18.7%). Missing values are not automatically defects: add information only when it is supported by a reliable source and useful for learners.
- The 338/809 related-term entries without a definition are an editorial enrichment queue, not a reason to invent meanings.

### Listening and reading

- Listening inventory: 121 units / 239 questions. Current Mock-eligible pool: 102; independent-review pending: 137. Only one complete 100-question Listening form can be assembled without reusing question IDs; a second form would reuse 98 questions at the current eligible count.
- By Part: eligible P1/P2/P3/P4 = 8/25/39/30; pending = 1/28/60/48. The Part 1 learning-outcome tracker has a 10-unique-question practice threshold, while one Listening mock blueprint uses 6 Part 1 questions. These are different thresholds. Two non-repeating full forms require 12 Part 1 questions; even after all currently pending questions are approved, the bank would have 9 and remain short by 3.
- Reading inventory: 65 resources / 263 questions. The Part 7 bank contains 86 single-passage and 85 multiple-passage questions. Second review remains a separate editorial gate.
- Separate Part 5 practice has 80 questions and remains practice-only pending independent review. Supplementary Foundation A2 Listening/Reading (39 questions each) also remains review-pending. Automated structure checks do not approve these items for Mock use.

## 7. Recommendations for the project owner

1. **Visual style:** approve `Calm Study Blue` as the initial shared design profile. It already exists as a proposed 54-token profile; approval should follow a real browser review. No profile status has been changed by this release.
2. **Listening Mock target:** recommend a minimum of **two distinct, non-repeating 100-question forms** before describing the Listening Mock bank as broadly ready. This requires independent review of suitable pending items and at least three more approved Part 1 questions beyond the projected nine. Until then, label current capability as one eligible form, not two.
3. **Foundation / Sound Lab / outcome tracker vs vocabulary:** keep existing modules and learner evidence; do not delete them or discard work. Freeze expansion of new feature surfaces for now and prioritize (a) independent review of Listening/Reading/Part 5/Foundation reserves, then (b) vocabulary batches of 100–150 with reliable-source evidence and controlled patches. Do not fill metadata fields merely to reach 100%.

These are recommendations, not silent changes to approved scope. The design-profile status and the two-form target remain owner decisions. Detailed regenerated inventories are in `TOEIC_CONTENT_COVERAGE_v2.95.10.md`, `TOEIC_LISTENING_READINESS_v2.95.10.md` and `PROJECT_PROGRESS_SNAPSHOT_v2.95.10.md`.

# Foundation A2 Assessment Quality Pass — v2.95.39

## Scope
- 13 core A2 Reading resources + 13 core A2 Listening resources; the new 13 supplementary A2 Listening clips (39 questions) are separately scoped and pending independent review.
- Focused review of within-resource q2/q3 repetition, answer-key uniqueness, four-choice integrity and explicit source traceability for changed/retained focus questions.
- Five question prompts/answer tasks were materially revised; six reviewed question records now carry exact source-evidence pointers.

## Automated integrity results
| Bank | A2 resources | A2 questions | A2 answer positions A/B/C/D |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Reading | 13 | 39 | 10 / 10 / 10 / 9 |
| Listening | 13 | 39 | 10 / 10 / 10 / 9 |

- All A2 questions require four unique choices, a valid answer index, a non-empty prompt and rationale.
- Each A2 resource must have three questions with non-identical q2/q3 correct answers.
- Each source-evidence pointer is checked as an exact substring of its Reading passage or spoken Listening segment.
- Core Reading answer positions remain A/B/C/D = 15/15/15/14; Listening full bank including supplementary practice is A/B/C/D = 25/25/24/24.
- Existing A2 q1/q2 objects remain protected by the v2.75.0 canonical-hash baseline tests.

## Focused changes
| Question | Change |
|---|---|
| `a2-quantities::reading1::q3` | Replaced q3 with a consequence/inference question about the delivery timing and preparation of training materials. |
| `a2-comparisons::reading1::q3` | Replaced q3 with an inference about the customer's priority: dependable, on-time delivery versus lowest price. |
| `a2-obligation-permission::reading1::q3` | Replaced q3 with the separate departure requirement to return the visitor badge. |
| `a2-comparisons::listening1::q3` | Reworded q3 to test the stated reliability/on-time advantage; q2 remains byte-identical to the v2.75.0 baseline. |
| `a2-sequencing-instructions::listening1::q3` | Replaced q3 with the immediately preceding action before preparing the return label. |

## Review boundary
- The pass fixes five identified cases of repeated information and records six exact source pointers. It does not certify every distractor for semantic plausibility or uniqueness.
- The work is an internal single-author review. Independent second-person language review and psychometric validation remain pending.
- The local A2 three-question / 67% rule is a practice threshold only; it is not a CEFR standard, mastery declaration or ETS equivalence.

## Automated audit status
- **PASS** — all registered structural, source-evidence, pair-distinction and answer-position checks passed.

| Bank | Items pending | Resources | Required review |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Listening Parts 1–4 | 161 | 73 units | Source/key fit, response fit, distractor uniqueness; P1 photo/action match |
| Reading Part 7 | 87 | 22 resources | Document evidence, inference, cross-document links, one-best-answer uniqueness |
| Separate Part 5 sentence completion | 80 | 1 bank | Grammar, naturalness, distractors, translation and one-answer uniqueness |

## Reviewer record

- Reviewer name / role: ____________________________________
- Review date: _____________________________________________
- Review method / reference material: ________________________
- Decision key: `APPROVE` / `REVISE` / `REJECT` (record per item; do not approve a whole batch by default).
- For approval: confirm one defensible key, all distractors are wrong in context, source evidence supports the key, and explanation/translation are accurate.
- For revision: record the exact field and proposed correction; keep the item out of Mock until the correction is retested.

## A. Listening reserve

For Part 2, assess speech act, polarity, indirect response and naturalness. For Parts 3–4, assess transcript support and distractor plausibility. For Part 1, inspect the photo itself as well as the spoken statements.

### Part 1 · `part1-office-cleaning` · Sweeping an office hallway

- Batch: `017` · Status: `reserve-pending-independent-review`
- Transcript: A maintenance worker is sweeping the floor in a hallway. A cleaner is wiping the glass doors with a cloth. A worker is pushing a cleaning cart down the corridor. Several chairs are being arranged near the entrance.
- Spoken-statement translation / A–D mapping: A. Một nhân viên bảo trì đang quét sàn hành lang. B. Một nhân viên vệ sinh đang lau cửa kính bằng khăn. C. Một công nhân đang đẩy xe vệ sinh dọc hành lang. D. Một số chiếc ghế đang được sắp xếp gần lối vào.
- Photo: `./assets/listening/part1-office-cleaning.jpg` · Alt: A maintenance worker is sweeping the tiled floor of an office hallway with a broom. A cleaning cart stands nearby.
- Internal visual note (not independent approval): Image check: the worker is visibly using a broom to sweep the tiled hallway floor; the cleaning cart is stationary beside him. The image does not show wiping the glass doors, pushing the cart, or arranging chairs. This is an internal visual check, not independent certification.

**Q1. Listen to the four statements and select the one that best describes the photograph.**

- Choices: **A. Option A**<br>B. Option B<br>C. Option C<br>D. Option D
- Current keyed answer: **A. Option A**
- Source pointer: A maintenance worker is sweeping the floor in a hallway.
- Current explanation: Đáp án A: Người công nhân đang dùng chổi quét sàn hành lang. Xe vệ sinh chỉ đang đặt bên cạnh, không được đẩy đi. Ảnh không cho thấy người này lau cửa kính hoặc sắp xếp ghế.

## C. Separate TOEIC Part 5 sentence-completion reserve

This 80-question bank is separate from Reading Part 5 and must not be counted as Mock-eligible. Check the complete sentence, grammar focus, distractors, translation and every option explanation.

### `p5-sc-001` · Infinitives and Verb Patterns

- Sentence: The HR manager asked all new employees to __________ the orientation form by Friday.
- Choices: **A. complete**<br>B. completion<br>C. completely<br>D. completed
- Current keyed answer: **A. complete**
- Grammar point: Verb pattern: ask + object + to-infinitive
- Single-answer rationale: “to” đứng ngay trước chỗ trống nên chỉ động từ nguyên mẫu “complete” phù hợp; các lựa chọn còn lại là danh từ, trạng từ hoặc quá khứ phân từ.
- Vietnamese translation: Quản lý nhân sự yêu cầu tất cả nhân viên mới hoàn thành biểu mẫu định hướng trước thứ Sáu.

- Single-answer rationale: “Supervising” là phân từ hiện tại phù hợp với nghĩa chủ động và chức năng bổ nghĩa cho “technician”.
- Vietnamese translation: Kỹ thuật viên đang giám sát ca đêm phải hoàn thành nhật ký an toàn trước khi rời đi.

### `p5-sc-073` · Infinitives and Verb Patterns

- Sentence: The new recognition program is designed to __________ employees to share practical ideas.
- Choices: A. encouraging<br>B. encouragement<br>**C. encourage**<br>D. encouraged
- Current keyed answer: **C. encourage**
- Grammar point: Be designed to + base verb
- Single-answer rationale: Sau “to” của cụm “be designed to” cần động từ nguyên mẫu “encourage”.
- Vietnamese translation: Chương trình ghi nhận mới được thiết kế nhằm khuyến khích nhân viên chia sẻ các ý tưởng thiết thực.

### `p5-sc-074` · Infinitives and Verb Patterns

- Sentence: Managers must __________ that all visitors sign in at reception.
- Choices: A. ensuring<br>B. ensures<br>C. ensured<br>**D. ensure**
- Current keyed answer: **D. ensure**
- Grammar point: Modal verb + base form
- Single-answer rationale: “Ensure” là dạng nguyên mẫu duy nhất đi sau “must”; các lựa chọn khác sai dạng động từ.
- Vietnamese translation: Các quản lý phải bảo đảm tất cả khách đến thăm đăng ký tại quầy lễ tân.

- Sentence: Please forward the signed contract __________ the legal department for review.
- Choices: **A. to**<br>B. at<br>C. for<br>D. with

- Grammar point: Forward something to a recipient
- Single-answer rationale: “To the legal department” xác định đích đến của tài liệu; các giới từ còn lại không thể hiện quan hệ chuyển tiếp này.

# Robot Buddy — v2.95.9 progressive replies and local composition

## User-visible changes

- A submitted message first shows the three-dot “đang chuẩn bị câu trả lời” indicator.
- The reply then appears progressively by grapheme-sized chunks, with a blinking caret. The caret and typing animation respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- The user can send another message while a reply is streaming; the previous partial response is safely completed before the new turn is appended.
- Reply action buttons appear only after the streamed text completes.
- The feature/help flow retains its shortcuts, and current-page/current-item content remains available to the response composer.

## Less rigid local responses

- Feature guidance combines a varied opener, an authored feature explanation and a varied action prompt.
- FAQ answers use phrase-scored matching and varied framing/closing text.
- Current-item help uses the active page, item title and available snippet, with varied transitions and study steps.
- Identity, encouragement and clarification messages are assembled from independent local phrase groups.
- Repeated supported prompts can receive different phrasing even when the underlying factual guidance is unchanged.
- Unknown prompts are handled honestly: the Buddy asks what topic or task the learner means and may refer to the current item; it does not invent a factual answer.

## Technical and privacy boundary

- This is not ChatGPT and does not use a generative model. The streaming effect animates locally composed text; it does not stream from an AI service.
- Content sources are the bundled dialogue/FAQ library, light rule-based intent classification, varied response fragments and the current in-memory app context.
- No external API, backend, WebSocket, remote model, new permission or analytics service was added.
- The Buddy itself still does not open IndexedDB/localStorage. Learning Insights remain opt-in and read-only through the app-supplied in-memory snapshot. No progress is written, reset, migrated or transmitted.
- Existing Learning Insights dashboard, shortcut actions, Placement consent/skip, idle reminders and head-only mascot are preserved.

## Acceptance checks

1. Send “Mở Từ vựng”: see the thinking dots, then progressive text and a blinking caret; the route shortcut appears after completion.
2. Open a vocabulary word and ask “Giải thích từ này giúp tôi”: reply must include the current word/available meaning and context-specific study guidance.
3. Repeat the same supported request: phrasing should vary while preserving the same supported guidance.
4. Ask an unsupported question: Buddy should request clarification, not fabricate an answer.
5. Start a second message mid-stream: the first reply must complete cleanly; no overlapping cursor or stale timer remains.
6. Enable OS reduced-motion: Buddy should render the complete response without the typing animation.
7. Toggle Learning Insights off/on: normal local conversation continues; the insight dashboard remains opt-in and read-only.
8. Test offline: conversation/composition works without external network calls.

Browser visual acceptance, deployed Pages behavior, offline installation and physical-device performance remain pending until checked after deployment.
<!-- END ARCHIVED-DOCUMENT: docs/reports/ROBOT_BUDDY_v2.95.9.md -->

## Answer-position distribution — balanced with stable choice identity
| Part | A | B | C | D | Total |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Part 3 | 10 | 10 | 10 | 9 | 39 |

**Rebalancing method:** 27 question groups had only the keyed option exchanged with a distractor position: 8 in Part 3, 5 in Part 4 and 14 in Part 7. The answer text, source evidence, explanation, question IDs and question order were retained. Each changed question carries `previousChoices` and `previousChoiceIds` from v2.16.0; the matching `choiceIds` moved with the option. At startup, progress containing a v2.16 `choiceId` is relocated to its new index; older records without an ID are mapped through the v2.16 snapshot. The prior index is preserved in `previousChoiceIndex`. No random shuffle was used.

## Quality decision and remaining limitations
- The 12 revised groups now use distractors closer to the same document purpose, role, travel record, service request, business action or visitor-access context. The correct answer text and `answerIndex` were kept unchanged for every revised question.
- Historical reviewed groups were retained where the three alternatives are distinct and the transcript/passage supports one clear key. For the new v2.92.0 and v2.93.0 Part 7 groups, close dates/times, locations, delivery steps and document-purpose alternatives were authored to be plausible, but an independent reviewer must confirm that exactly one option is defensible.
- Listening reserve total: 137 questions across 65 units. This script structurally checks Part 3/4 reserve blocks; Part 2 response-fit is tracked separately. Structural checks never approve a reserve for Mock.
- This is editorial review of original-authored content. It is not official ETS content, two-person independent review, statistical item analysis, difficulty calibration or proof of score equivalence.
- Part 1 uses source-tracked licensed Pexels and AI-generated photographs with a JPG-only runtime contract; Listening audio remains browser SpeechSynthesis. Physical-device audio/voice review is still pending.

# TOEIC Editorial Evidence Audit — v2.95.34

## Scope and interpretation
- Questions indexed: **550** (263 Listening + 287 Reading).
- Every correct option is linked to its source transcript/passage or an explicit review category.
- Direct/lexical matching is evidence discovery only. It does not prove that distractors are wrong or that a paraphrase/inference is unique.
- Editorial review categories recorded in this source: 6 manually checked low-overlap paraphrase/inference items; 8 Part 1 image/action items; 25 Part 2 response-fit items; 60 Part 5 grammar items; and 32 Part 6 context/cohesion items.
- 161 Listening questions remain reserve-pending-independent-review (Part 1: 1, Part 2: 28, Part 3: 72, Part 4: 60). All reserve answers and distractor uniqueness still require an independent second reviewer; automated evidence mapping does not approve them.
- Reserve traceability gate: **161/161** questions have a transcript evidence pointer that matches the source (0 missing/broken); Part 1 visual evidence note recorded for 1 pending photo item(s).
- Traceable evidence is a review aid, not proof that the key is correct, the distractors are uniquely wrong or the item is ready for Mock.
- These are internal editorial checks, not two-person independent proofreading, psychometric validation or ETS approval.

- Focused Python tests: **76 test executions (73 unique tests; 3 repeat executions)** across 14 distinct suites (new explanation context, choice identity/history, practice fallback, CI coverage/repository integrity, and related-glossary batches 021/022/023/026/027/028/030/032).

- `tools/validate-learning-content.py`: PASS, 0 errors/0 warnings.
- `tools/audit-repository-integrity.py`: PASS, 408 local references/data files inspected, 0 errors/optional warnings.
- `tools/sync-version.py --check`: PASS.

## Package verification
- FullSource: **559 files**.
- Patch: **12 files (9 changed + 3 added), 0 deleted**.
- Replay onto v2.95.37: **559/559 byte-for-byte match**.
- ZIP CRC, single root, excluded-path check and SHA-256: PASS.

## Not verified
- Full Python unittest discovery not run in this release.
- Remote GitHub Actions, Pages deployment, real browser/device acceptance not run.

## Data safety
No vocabulary meanings, relation arrays, question/answer keys, learner progress, IndexedDB schema or UI layout were changed.

# TOEIC Dictionary — Project Progress Snapshot v2.95.15

- Candidate source: v2.95.15; baseline v2.95.14 (`e269173`).
- Release type: sourced related-term glossary addition plus CI/regression maintenance; local-only candidate.
- Claude's v2.95.13 review remains pending and will be reconciled when the owner shares the result.

## Inventory and status

| Area | Current value | Status |
|---|---:|---|
| Canonical vocabulary | 1,141 headwords | Stable IDs preserved; no new headword in this release |
| Related-term glossary | 387 entries | 4 new glosses in batch 022; independent lexical review pending |
| Synonym/antonym exact join | 376/804 | 428 distinct terms / 465 occurrences remain unglossed |
| Listening | 121 units / 239 questions | 102 eligible / 137 reserve pending independent review |
| Reading | 65 resources / 263 questions | Part 7 second-review gate remains |
| Grammar | 50 lessons / 137 exercises | Retained |
| Separate Part 5 practice | 80 questions | Practice-only; independent review pending |
| Foundation pathway | 23 lessons | Core and supplementary A2 scope unchanged |

## v2.95.15 completed

- Added `aim`, `avoid`, `cause` and `conceal` with POS-scoped, Cambridge-linked glosses.
- Applied an absent-only SHA-256-guarded patch and verified rollback against the exact baseline file hash.
- Added batch 022 provenance, 9 dedicated Python tests, CI execution and JS release-integrity assertions.
- Local verification: 36/36 focused Python cases, 38/38 JavaScript suites, all source syntax checks and three data/repository validators PASS.

## Open gates

- Independent lexical review for all glossary additions remains pending.
- 22 owner-run manual acceptance rows remain Chưa kiểm.
- Remote Actions/Pages and browser/device acceptance remain unverified.
- Full Python aggregate was not completed.

## Recommended next focus

Continue glossary completion only where frequency and contextual need justify it; the next remaining terms each have at most two current relationship references. In parallel, prioritize review of the 93 missing US IPA entries and the existing word-family/verb-form backlog. Do not inflate data counts by adding low-value one-off synonyms.

## Quality / verification status

- Content counts do not equal completed learning outcomes.
- Outcome framework: 33/33 criteria defined; 6/33 have an evidence-collection path. Neither count measures learner mastery.
- TOEIC objective tracker: aggregates latest answer per stable unique question; minimum 10 unique items and 80% accuracy. A passing label is a practice threshold only, not CEFR/ETS certification or proof of every outcome.
- Objective evidence is connected for Grammar, Listening Parts 1–4, Reading Parts 5–7 and separate Part 5 practice. Reserve Listening items are excluded until editorial review; Reading Part 7 remains second-review-gated; the separate 80-item Part 5 practice pool is review-pending and cannot earn a threshold status.
- Listening Part 1 currently has 8 eligible unique questions (one additional mapped item is reserve-pending), below the 10-item minimum; at least 2 more unique, reviewed questions are needed before it can reach the practice threshold.
- Foundation outcome evidence now records recognition, a learner-authored sentence with three self-report explanation/production ratings, and delayed recall. Self-report is not auto-graded; delayed recall is scheduled 1/3 days and is not a retention guarantee.
- Foundation Listening stores attempts under a separate localStorage key; its bank coverage does not imply the learner has completed the questions or met the local practice threshold.
- Supplementary A2 Listening has 13 six-turn dialogues (75–100 words each), 39 questions across detail, purpose/context and inference/next-action, with exact source-evidence snippets; all remain pending independent review and use browser TTS.
- v2.92.0 batch 024 adds 8 Grammar lessons / 24 exercises, 6 TOEIC Listening units / 18 questions, and 6 TOEIC Reading Part 7 resources / 27 questions. All 12 new Listening/Reading resources remain reserve-pending-independent-review and excluded from Mock eligibility. v2.93.0 batch 025 adds 9 Grammar lessons / 27 exercises, 8 TOEIC Listening units / 20 questions, 8 TOEIC Reading Part 7 resources / 36 questions and 4 vocabulary headwords; new Listening/Reading items remain pending independent review and Mock-excluded.
- Foundation A–Z records TTS play-button actions in `toeic:alphabet-sound-progress:v1`; no pronunciation analysis or mastery inference is performed.
- Part 5 practice: pending independent review; do not count as Mock-eligible.
- Listening pending-review pool and Mock-eligible counts must be tracked separately from raw inventory.
- Placement is a short sample, not official CEFR/ETS certification.
- TOEIC score readiness is a local evidence tracker based on three completed 200-question Full Mocks; it shows L/R practice-accuracy trends only and does not convert raw accuracy into ETS scaled scores or claim 500+/850+ readiness.
- Remote CI, GitHub Pages deployment and physical-device QA are not inferred from local checks.

## Reporting rule

A percentage is shown only when a defensible target or denominator exists. Otherwise the report says “Chưa đo được” and records the current inventory without inventing a target.

# Change Manifest — TOEIC Dictionary v2.95.19

## Baseline and candidate

- Baseline source: v2.95.18 FullSource.
- Candidate: v2.95.19.
- Scope: close Listening evidence-pointer gaps; make pending review states explicit; consolidate independent-review handoff; improve progress reporting and CI coverage.

## Data changes

| Area | Change | Guard / boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Listening Part 1–4 reserve records | Added matching `evidenceText` to 29 older questions whose evidence field was missing. | Transcript spans must match exact source text; all reserve statuses stay pending. |
| Listening Part 1 image item | Added `visualEvidenceNote` describing the visible broom/sweeping action. | Explicitly internal visual note; not a second reviewer approval. |
| Listening unit review metadata | Added explicit pending-review notes to 16 legacy units. | No change to `editorialStatus`; all 137 questions remain reserve-pending. |
| Reviewer handoff | Generated a single 280-question queue: 137 Listening, 63 Reading Part 7 and 80 Part 5. | Handoff only; no Mock eligibility or content status changed. |

## Tooling and tests

- Updated `tools/audit-question-evidence.py` to distinguish source-pointer traceability from correctness or editorial approval.
- Added `tools/build-editorial-review-queue.py` and `tools/tests/test_editorial_review_queue.py`.
- Added regression checks for all Listening reserve evidence pointers and review-queue ID coverage.
- Registered review queue compile/test steps in `.github/workflows/validate-data.yml`.
- Updated `tools/report-project-progress.py` to dynamically report pending review counts and the 280-item total; updated its tests and generated `PROJECT_PROGRESS_SNAPSHOT_v2.95.19.md`.
- Updated the release-integrity test to assert the current manifest version rather than the previous fixed release string.
- Restored the historical `docs/archive/PROJECT_HISTORY.md` reference required by the existing distractor-quality test.

## Explicit non-changes

- No visual redesign, CSS/layout refactor, navigation change or new UI module.
- No vocabulary headword, stable ID, IPA, definition, synonym/antonym relation or word-family content change.
- No Listening/Reading/Part 5 prompt, choices, answer key or explanation changed as part of this release.
- No learner progress, localStorage key, IndexedDB schema, backend or runtime API change.
- No pending reserve item promoted to Mock.
- No GitHub push or deployment.

## Files of interest

- `data/listening/listening-library.json`
- `tools/audit-question-evidence.py`
- `tools/build-editorial-review-queue.py`
- `tools/report-project-progress.py`

# Change Manifest — TOEIC Dictionary v2.95.21

## Baseline and candidate

- Baseline: recovered **v2.95.20 FullSource**.
- Candidate: **v2.95.21**, local source candidate; not pushed or deployed.
- Intent: continue the existing related-term lookup glossary expansion and close a stale progress-test expectation without abandoning the current review backlog.
- UI/CSS/layout/navigation/runtime feature development remains frozen for this content-focused release.

## Data changes

| Area | Change | Guard / boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Related-term glossary Batch 027 | Added 23 Vietnamese lookup glosses: `activity`, `answer`, `carry out`, `combination`, `common`, `continue`, `decrease`, `employee`, `funding`, `goal`, `inaction`, `make`, `minor`, `objective`, `oppose`, `send`, `study`, `support`, `work`, `maximum`, `different`, `determine`, `approach`. | Each term already occurs exactly twice in canonical synonym/antonym relations; each record includes Cambridge Dictionary source URL; additions remain provisional pending independent lexical review. |
| Glossary coverage | Count rises from 400 to 423; exact case-insensitive join rises 389/804 → 412/804 (51.2%); occurrence join rises 598/1,037 → 644/1,037 (62.1%). | 392 distinct terms / 393 relationship occurrences remain unglossed; inventory is not an editorial accuracy score. |
| Patch safety | Added absent-only patch and provenance ledger with the exact baseline file SHA-256. | Patch refuses to overwrite an existing term; dry-run and application were checked against the v2.95.20 baseline. |

## Tooling, tests and documentation

- Added `patches-related-terms/v2.95.21/related-terms-027.json` and `batch-027-glossary-ledger.json`.
- Added `tools/tests/test_related_glossary_batch_027.py` (5 regression tests).
- Updated `.github/workflows/validate-data.yml` to run the new suite and compile the new test module.
- Extended `tools/tests/vocabulary-release-integrity.mjs` to cover the new glossary batches and current 423-entry total.
- Repaired the stale expected coverage in `tools/tests/test_project_progress.py`; regenerated `docs/reports/PROJECT_PROGRESS_SNAPSHOT_v2.95.21.md` from canonical data.
- Restored `docs/archive/PROJECT_HISTORY.md`, a compact retired-document index required by the existing distractor-quality regression; updated the Master Status, current-version pointer, documentation index, and changelog without deleting historical release notes.
- Regenerated the v2.95.21 independent review queue and editorial evidence audit; the 280-question queue remains a handoff only.

## Explicit non-changes

- No canonical vocabulary headword, stable ID, synonym/antonym relation, word-family relation, IPA, learning question, answer key, explanation, learner record, localStorage key or IndexedDB schema changed.
- No UI redesign, CSS/layout/navigation, flashcard, listening playback, TTS, Robot Buddy, PWA service-worker behavior, backend or runtime API change.
- No reserve Listening/Reading/Part 5 item was promoted to Mock eligibility.
- No GitHub push, GitHub Actions remote run or Pages deployment was performed.

## Main files

- `data/related-terms.json`
- `patches-related-terms/v2.95.21/related-terms-027.json`
- `patches-related-terms/v2.95.21/batch-027-glossary-ledger.json`
- `tools/tests/test_related_glossary_batch_027.py`
- `tools/tests/test_project_progress.py`
- `tools/tests/vocabulary-release-integrity.mjs`
- `.github/workflows/validate-data.yml`
- `docs/reports/PROJECT_PROGRESS_SNAPSHOT_v2.95.21.md`
- `docs/reports/VOCABULARY_GLOSSARY_EXPANSION_v2.95.21.md`
- `docs/reports/TOEIC_INDEPENDENT_REVIEW_QUEUE_v2.95.21.md`
- `docs/reports/TOEIC_EDITORIAL_EVIDENCE_AUDIT_v2.95.21.md`

## Release gate

50 focused Python tests across nine modules and all 38 JavaScript suites pass. Python compile and domain validators pass. Full aggregate Python unittest discovery did not complete within the 240-second execution window and must remain marked incomplete. Remote CI, browser acceptance, physical-device QA, owner manual acceptance and independent lexical/editorial sign-off remain open.

# Release comparison — v2.95.5 vs v2.95.7 and v2.95.8 decision

## v2.95.5

- Contains the five regression groups delivered over v2.95.1–v2.95.5.
- Preserves Robot Buddy's optional local read-only Learning Insights, the visual dashboard and its toggle.
- Contains 34 JavaScript regression suites and 54 Python test modules, including the original release-rotation utility/test. Its original rotation helper did not protect older reports referenced by active documentation.

## v2.95.7

- Based on v2.95.6 and applies a corrective privacy change: removes `robot-learning-insights.js`, the app's snapshot adapter, progress dashboard, analysis toggle, progress-based idle nudges and their regression suites.
- Preserves the head-only mascot, static dialogue library, Placement consent/skip, quick prompts, reminders, feature shortcuts and interaction/idle safeguards.
- Improves documentation consolidation and strengthens the existing release-document rotation utility with reference protection, dry-run-first behavior and regression tests.
- Its ZIP contains 74 generated `.pyc` files under `__pycache__`; these are build/runtime artifacts, not source and must not ship.
- Its local report records 33/33 JavaScript suites PASS and 53/54 Python modules completed; `test_validator.py` was not completed within that run window.

## v2.95.8 selection

The v2.95.8 merge also makes the non-sensitive app-context behavior more useful: the Buddy receives the current page and current learning item (not a learner profile) for context-aware guidance and idle suggestions.

| Area | Decision |
|---|---|
| Five defect fixes | Keep all from v2.95.5 |
| Robot Buddy Learning Insights | Keep opt-in, local, read-only snapshot analysis and the single visual dashboard; do not import v2.95.7's feature removal |
| Static dialogue, Placement onboarding, quick prompts, reminder/idle safeguards | Keep |
| Documentation consolidation | Adopt the v2.95.7 Master / Compatibility / README structure |
| Release report rotation | Adopt the v2.95.7 dry-run-first script and regression test; preserve referenced active review handoffs |
| Generated bytecode | Exclude all `__pycache__`, `.pyc` and `.pyo` files |
| Compatibility tombstones | Keep `learning-assistant.js` and `quick-help.js` as inert overlay-compatibility files; do not reactivate them |

## Verification boundary

v2.95.8 retains the 34 JavaScript suites and 54 Python test modules, strengthens release rotation to protect relative links in Master/README/CHANGELOG, and re-runs the complete local suites and repository/content audits. GitHub Actions, GitHub Pages deployment, physical-device layout, offline/reconnect and actual audible TTS remain external acceptance gates.
<!-- END ARCHIVED-DOCUMENT: docs/reports/RELEASE_COMPARISON_v2.95.5_vs_v2.95.7_v2.95.8.md -->

# TOEIC Independent Editorial Review Queue — v2.95.25

> Mục đích: chuyển nội dung reserve cho người rà soát độc lập. Đây là phiếu làm việc, không phải chứng nhận đã duyệt. Không đổi `editorialStatus` sang `approved-for-mock` cho đến khi reviewer ghi quyết định và ngày rà soát.

## Queue summary

| Bank | Items pending | Resources | Required review |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Listening Parts 1–4 | 137 | 65 units | Source/key fit, response fit, distractor uniqueness; P1 photo/action match |
| Reading Part 7 | 63 | 14 resources | Document evidence, inference, cross-document links, one-best-answer uniqueness |
| Separate Part 5 sentence completion | 80 | 1 bank | Grammar, naturalness, distractors, translation and one-answer uniqueness |
| **Total** | **280** | **80** | **Independent review required** |

## Reviewer record

- Reviewer name / role: ____________________________________
- Review date: _____________________________________________
- Review method / reference material: ________________________
- Decision key: `APPROVE` / `REVISE` / `REJECT` (record per item; do not approve a whole batch by default).
- For approval: confirm one defensible key, all distractors are wrong in context, source evidence supports the key, and explanation/translation are accurate.
- For revision: record the exact field and proposed correction; keep the item out of Mock until the correction is retested.

## A. Listening reserve

For Part 2, assess speech act, polarity, indirect response and naturalness. For Parts 3–4, assess transcript support and distractor plausibility. For Part 1, inspect the photo itself as well as the spoken statements.

### Part 1 · `part1-office-cleaning` · Sweeping an office hallway

- Batch: `017` · Status: `reserve-pending-independent-review`
- Transcript: A maintenance worker is sweeping the floor in a hallway. A cleaner is wiping the glass doors with a cloth. A worker is pushing a cleaning cart down the corridor. Several chairs are being arranged near the entrance.
- Spoken-statement translation / A–D mapping: A. Một nhân viên bảo trì đang quét sàn hành lang. B. Một nhân viên vệ sinh đang lau cửa kính bằng khăn. C. Một công nhân đang đẩy xe vệ sinh dọc hành lang. D. Một số chiếc ghế đang được sắp xếp gần lối vào.
- Photo: `./assets/listening/part1-office-cleaning.jpg` · Alt: A maintenance worker is sweeping the tiled floor of an office hallway with a broom. A cleaning cart stands nearby.
- Internal visual note (not independent approval): Image check: the worker is visibly using a broom to sweep the tiled hallway floor; the cleaning cart is stationary beside him. The image does not show wiping the glass doors, pushing the cart, or arranging chairs. This is an internal visual check, not independent certification.

**Q1. Listen to the four statements and select the one that best describes the photograph.**

- Choices: **A. Option A**<br>B. Option B<br>C. Option C<br>D. Option D
- Current keyed answer: **A. Option A**
- Source pointer: A maintenance worker is sweeping the floor in a hallway.
- Current explanation: Đáp án A: Người công nhân đang dùng chổi quét sàn hành lang. Xe vệ sinh chỉ đang đặt bên cạnh, không được đẩy đi. Ảnh không cho thấy người này lau cửa kính hoặc sắp xếp ghế.
- Reviewer: [ ] source supports key  [ ] response/action fits  [ ] distractors are clearly wrong  [ ] only one defensible answer
- Decision: `________` · Correction / notes: __________________________________________

### Part 2 · `part2-monitor-delivery-arrival` · Replacement monitor delivery

- Batch: `legacy` · Status: `reserve-pending-independent-review`
- Transcript: Has the replacement monitor arrived yet?
- Transcript translation: Màn hình thay thế đã được giao đến chưa? — Chưa; đơn vị chuyển phát dự kiến giao sau bữa trưa.

**Q1. Choose the most appropriate response.**

- Choices: A. The monitor has a wider screen.<br>**B. Not yet; the courier expects it after lunch.**<br>C. I ordered a desk lamp last week.
- Current keyed answer: **B. Not yet; the courier expects it after lunch.**
- Source pointer: Has the replacement monitor arrived yet?
- Current explanation: Câu hỏi Has ... arrived yet? hỏi tình trạng hàng đã đến hay chưa. “Not yet” trả lời trực tiếp và mốc sau bữa trưa cung cấp thời gian dự kiến. Hai lựa chọn còn lại nói về đặc điểm thiết bị và một đơn hàng khác.
- Reviewer: [ ] source supports key  [ ] response/action fits  [ ] distractors are clearly wrong  [ ] only one defensible answer

# Vocabulary Sense Expansion — v2.95.13

## Scope and baseline

- Baseline source: v2.95.12, Git commit `85be68a`.
- Candidate: v2.95.13 (local candidate; not deployed).
- Canonical inventory stays at 1,141 headwords across A–Z.
- All data edits were generated by strict patch tools. No `id`, `word` or `topics` field was changed. The stable ID set SHA-256 remains `adccbdb4c98872207d2bede7bdc530e1c079bbd8b3679e7e4f6288054c7e404b`.
- Added/adjusted meanings and supporting glosses are provisional and **pending independent lexical review**. Cambridge Dictionary references are provenance, not a claim of second-person approval.

## Ten existing headwords with clearer meanings

| Headword | Distinctions recorded | Senses | Examples |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| `bill` | noun: amount/document owed; verb: send a payment statement | 2 | 2 |
| `charge` | noun: fee; verb: ask for payment; verb: put electrical energy into a device | 3 | 3 |
| `document` | noun: paper/electronic information file; verb: record details | 2 | 2 |
| `experience` | noun: acquired knowledge/skill; noun: an event affecting someone; verb: undergo/feel | 3 | 3 |
| `function` | noun: purpose/duty; verb: work or operate | 2 | 2 |
| `host` | noun: person/organization receiving guests or providing event venue; verb: host an event | 2 | 2 |
| `minute` | noun: one-sixtieth of an hour; noun: written meeting record (`minutes`) | 2 | 2 |
| `offer` | noun: proposal; verb: express willingness to give/do; verb: provide a product/service/opportunity | 3 | 3 |
| `supply` | noun: amount available; verb: provide what is needed | 2 | 2 |
| `value` | noun: monetary worth; verb: assess worth; verb: consider important | 3 | 3 |
| **Total additions** | **10 existing headwords** | **24 sense-linked examples** | **24** |

The overall project inventory increases from 39 to 49 multi-sense headwords and from 81 to 105 examples attached to multi-sense records. The added examples all carry a `sense_index` pointing to an existing sense.

## Supporting glossary and family-link consistency

- Added four Cambridge-sourced Vietnamese related-term glosses: `demand`, `guest`, `inexperience`, `refund`. `data/related-terms.json` now contains 373 terms (previously 369).
- Corrected the reverse family relation `valuable → value (n)` to use the monetary-worth noun sense.
- Corrected `valuation → value (v)` to use the assess-monetary-worth verb sense. This second correction followed a regression test that exposed the stale `n/v` relation after sense separation.

## Data patch trail

1. `patches/v2.95.13/batch-001.json` — 20 operations / 10 headwords; allowlists `/senses` and `/examples`; ID-set SHA-256 plus per-record identity guards.
2. `patches-related-terms/v2.95.13/related-terms-001.json` — four absent-term additions with a base-file SHA-256 precondition and Cambridge dictionary URLs.
3. `patches/v2.95.13/batch-002-family-gloss.json` — one exact `/word_family/0` operation for `valuable-adj`.
4. `patches/v2.95.13/batch-003-family-gloss.json` — one exact `/word_family/0` operation for `valuation-n`.
5. `data/vocabulary/batch-017.json` through `batch-020.json` — provenance snapshots for the sense, glossary and family-link additions.

Every vocabulary operation includes `expect.old`; each patch declares exact `allowedPaths`; stable IDs are locked by SHA-256 and identity guards. All patches were dry-run and applied from a clean v2.95.12 archive. The 10 changed letter files (`B`, `C`, `D`, `E`, `F`, `H`, `M`, `O`, `S`, `V`) and `related-terms.json` matched the candidate byte-for-byte after replay.

## Coverage snapshot

| Measure | v2.95.12 baseline | v2.95.13 candidate |
|---|---:|---:|
| Canonical headwords | 1,141 | 1,141 |
| Stable IDs | 1,141 | 1,141; 0 added / 0 missing |
| Multi-sense headwords | 39 | 49 |
| Examples attached to multi-sense records | 81 | 105 |
| Related-term glossary entries | 369 | 373 |

Field coverage remains an inventory metric, not editorial approval: US IPA 1,048/1,141; word-family records 276/1,141; verb-form records 329/1,141; collocations 971/1,141. The vocabulary validator's informational summary reports synonym/antonym occurrences lacking a glossary definition as 327/804; this is not interchangeable with a custom exact-term comparison.

## Review status and limitations

- All 10 sense expansions, 24 examples, four glossary entries and two family-link corrections remain provisional pending independent lexical review.
- The existing Flashcard helper renders additional senses and their linked examples; automated tests were run against the new records. A real-browser visual check is still required.
- No changes to question banks, answer keys, Mock eligibility, learner records, IndexedDB schema, localStorage keys, Robot Buddy logic or Service Worker behavior were made in this release.
- GitHub Actions, GitHub Pages deployment, browser visual layout, PWA/offline, two-tab updates and iOS/Android TTS remain unverified.

- Cambridge Dictionary — charge: https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/charge
- Cambridge Dictionary — document: https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/document
- Cambridge Dictionary — experience: https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/experience
- Cambridge Dictionary — function: https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/function

- Cambridge Dictionary — value: https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/value

# User Acceptance Checklist — v2.95.25

## Glossary source backfill
- [ ] Open vocabulary/review UI on a term that uses related-term fallback (e.g. `accept`, `accessible`, `record`).
- [ ] Confirm English definition is no longer the generic placeholder.
- [ ] Confirm Vietnamese gloss remains intact and POS is present.
- [ ] For multi-sense term `record`, confirm combined definitions are readable.
- [ ] Verify fallback/reference terms still work in practice; no duplicate choices or answer-key changes.

## Regression and environment checks
- [ ] iPhone Safari: open, refresh, and inspect vocabulary detail/fallback.
- [ ] Desktop browser at 100% zoom: confirm sidebar/footer still visible.
- [ ] Offline/reconnect: use previously cached shell; then reconnect and confirm no data loss.
- [ ] TTS: confirm actual device voice and cadence (not covered by automated test).
- [ ] Confirm no local vocabulary, review history or settings were reset.

Record device/browser, date, result and any screenshots before approving deployment.

# Foundation A2 Assessment Quality Pass — v2.95.40

## Scope
- 13 core A2 Reading resources + 13 core A2 Listening resources; the new 13 supplementary A2 Listening clips (39 questions) are separately scoped and pending independent review.
- Focused review of within-resource q2/q3 repetition, answer-key uniqueness, four-choice integrity and explicit source traceability for changed/retained focus questions.

## Quality / verification status

- Content counts do not equal completed learning outcomes.
- Outcome framework: 33/33 criteria defined; 6/33 have an evidence-collection path. Neither count measures learner mastery.
- TOEIC objective tracker: aggregates latest answer per stable unique question; minimum 10 unique items and 80% accuracy. A passing label is a practice threshold only, not CEFR/ETS certification or proof of every outcome.
- Objective evidence is connected for Grammar, Listening Parts 1–4, Reading Parts 5–7 and separate Part 5 practice. Reserve Listening items are excluded until editorial review; Reading Part 7 remains second-review-gated; the separate 80-item Part 5 practice pool is review-pending and cannot earn a threshold status.
- Listening Part 1 currently has 8 eligible unique questions (one additional mapped item is reserve-pending), below the 10-item minimum; at least 2 more unique, reviewed questions are needed before it can reach the practice threshold.
- Foundation outcome evidence now records recognition, a learner-authored sentence with three self-report explanation/production ratings, and delayed recall. Self-report is not auto-graded; delayed recall is scheduled 1/3 days and is not a retention guarantee.
- Foundation Listening stores attempts under a separate localStorage key; its bank coverage does not imply the learner has completed the questions or met the local practice threshold.
- Supplementary A2 Listening has 13 six-turn dialogues (75–100 words each), 39 questions across detail, purpose/context and inference/next-action, with exact source-evidence snippets; all remain pending independent review and use browser TTS.
- v2.92.0 batch 024 adds 8 Grammar lessons / 24 exercises, 6 TOEIC Listening units / 18 questions, and 6 TOEIC Reading Part 7 resources / 27 questions. All 12 new Listening/Reading resources remain reserve-pending-independent-review and excluded from Mock eligibility. v2.93.0 batch 025 adds 9 Grammar lessons / 27 exercises, 8 TOEIC Listening units / 20 questions, 8 TOEIC Reading Part 7 resources / 36 questions and 4 vocabulary headwords; new Listening/Reading items remain pending independent review and Mock-excluded.
- Foundation A–Z records TTS play-button actions in `toeic:alphabet-sound-progress:v1`; no pronunciation analysis or mastery inference is performed.
- Part 5 practice: pending independent review; do not count as Mock-eligible.
- Listening pending-review pool and Mock-eligible counts must be tracked separately from raw inventory.
- Placement is a short sample, not official CEFR/ETS certification.
- TOEIC score readiness is a local evidence tracker based on three completed 200-question Full Mocks; it shows L/R practice-accuracy trends only and does not convert raw accuracy into ETS scaled scores or claim 500+/850+ readiness.
- Remote CI, GitHub Pages deployment and physical-device QA are not inferred from local checks.

## Reporting rule

A percentage is shown only when a defensible target or denominator exists. Otherwise the report says “Chưa đo được” and records the current inventory without inventing a target.


## v2.95.8 Robot Buddy behavior boundary

- Robot Buddy retains the head-only mascot, static dialogue library, feature guidance, quick prompts, Placement consent/skip, reminder controls and idle safeguards.
- Optional Learning Insights uses an in-memory snapshot passed by the app from already-loaded local records. The aggregator is read-only and does not open IndexedDB/localStorage, write progress, migrate records or transmit data.
- Progress analysis appears as one visual dashboard; duplicate prose statistics are suppressed. It is not an ETS score prediction or proof of mastery.

1. Backfill only glossary placeholder definitions where an exact canonical headword and bilingual sense exists.

3. Improve IPA and morphology only with source-backed evidence; coverage percentage is not accuracy.
4. Complete independent review for reserve Listening, Reading Part 7 and separate Part 5 items before Mock eligibility changes.
5. Instrument learning outcomes only when an outcome-specific evidence mapping is defensible and regression-tested.
6. Run browser/device, offline/reconnect and remote CI acceptance before deployment.

- Questions indexed: **502** (239 Listening + 263 Reading).
- Every correct option is linked to its source transcript/passage or an explicit review category.
- Direct/lexical matching is evidence discovery only. It does not prove that distractors are wrong or that a paraphrase/inference is unique.
- Editorial review categories recorded in this source: 6 manually checked low-overlap paraphrase/inference items; 8 Part 1 image/action items; 25 Part 2 response-fit items; 60 Part 5 grammar items; and 32 Part 6 context/cohesion items.
- 137 Listening questions remain reserve-pending-independent-review (Part 1: 1, Part 2: 28, Part 3: 60, Part 4: 48). All reserve answers and distractor uniqueness still require an independent second reviewer; automated evidence mapping does not approve them.
- Reserve traceability gate: **137/137** questions have a transcript evidence pointer that matches the source (0 missing/broken); Part 1 visual evidence note recorded for 1 pending photo item(s).
- Traceable evidence is a review aid, not proof that the key is correct, the distractors are uniquely wrong or the item is ready for Mock.
- These are internal editorial checks, not two-person independent proofreading, psychometric validation or ETS approval.

# Foundation A2 Assessment Quality Pass — v2.95.35

## Scope
- 13 core A2 Reading resources + 13 core A2 Listening resources; the new 13 supplementary A2 Listening clips (39 questions) are separately scoped and pending independent review.
- Focused review of within-resource q2/q3 repetition, answer-key uniqueness, four-choice integrity and explicit source traceability for changed/retained focus questions.
- Five question prompts/answer tasks were materially revised; six reviewed question records now carry exact source-evidence pointers.

## Automated integrity results
| Bank | A2 resources | A2 questions | A2 answer positions A/B/C/D |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Reading | 13 | 39 | 10 / 10 / 10 / 9 |
| Listening | 13 | 39 | 10 / 10 / 10 / 9 |

- All A2 questions require four unique choices, a valid answer index, a non-empty prompt and rationale.
- Each A2 resource must have three questions with non-identical q2/q3 correct answers.
- Each source-evidence pointer is checked as an exact substring of its Reading passage or spoken Listening segment.
- Core Reading answer positions remain A/B/C/D = 15/15/15/14; Listening full bank including supplementary practice is A/B/C/D = 25/25/24/24.
- Existing A2 q1/q2 objects remain protected by the v2.75.0 canonical-hash baseline tests.

## Focused changes
| Question | Change |
|---|---|
| `a2-quantities::reading1::q3` | Replaced q3 with a consequence/inference question about the delivery timing and preparation of training materials. |
| `a2-comparisons::reading1::q3` | Replaced q3 with an inference about the customer's priority: dependable, on-time delivery versus lowest price. |
| `a2-obligation-permission::reading1::q3` | Replaced q3 with the separate departure requirement to return the visitor badge. |
| `a2-comparisons::listening1::q3` | Reworded q3 to test the stated reliability/on-time advantage; q2 remains byte-identical to the v2.75.0 baseline. |
| `a2-sequencing-instructions::listening1::q3` | Replaced q3 with the immediately preceding action before preparing the return label. |

## Review boundary
- The pass fixes five identified cases of repeated information and records six exact source pointers. It does not certify every distractor for semantic plausibility or uniqueness.
- The work is an internal single-author review. Independent second-person language review and psychometric validation remain pending.
- The local A2 three-question / 67% rule is a practice threshold only; it is not a CEFR standard, mastery declaration or ETS equivalence.

## Automated audit status
- **PASS** — all registered structural, source-evidence, pair-distinction and answer-position checks passed.

# Safe IPA backfill report — v2.95.31

## Change
- Canonical word `dispute` (`dispute-n`) received US IPA `/dɪ.ˈspjut/` from an exact CMUdict single-pronunciation entry, after conversion validation.
- Cumulative source-linked ledger now contains 334 records (up from 333).
- Missing US IPA decreased 80 → 79 (1,062/1,141 records have US IPA; 93%).
- Converter onset allowlist now includes the `spj` cluster so the glide remains attached to the stressed onset. Regression expectation: `D IH0 S P Y UW1 T` → `/dɪ.ˈspjut/`.

## Candidate review
- 80 previous missing records examined.
- 1 unique candidate passed converter and was applied.
- 5 unique candidates failed conversion (multi-primary stress) and remain review-only.
- 49 records have multiple CMUdict variants and remain review-only.
- 25 exact headwords are not present in CMUdict.

## New pipeline
`tools/backfill_missing_ipa_from_cmudict.py` is preview-only by default. `--apply` only adds exact, single-variant candidates that pass the converter; it never overwrites existing IPA. Case-insensitive dictionary-key normalization, duplicate variant collapse, stable queue ordering and failure-to-review routing are covered by 8 tests.

## Test limitations
The CMUdict-derived entry is not independent dictionary verification. CMUdict itself may contain errors and omissions; converter output is project-normalized IPA. Ambiguous and converter-failing candidates were not forced into canonical data. No physical-device test, GitHub Actions run or Pages deployment was performed.
